summary.headline: Redington's SSG unit grew 29% in USD to $2.2B in FY26 (17% of group revenue); management targets ~$5B revenue in three years at 5.5-6% gross margin.
summary.overview: This was a virtual investor event (held June 17, 2026) focused on Redington's Software Solutions Group (SSG), not a formal quarterly results call, so no reported Q4 FY26 P&L was presented. SSG grew about 29% in USD to a $2.2B business in FY26 (about 37% in INR terms) and now contributes 17% of group revenue, up from about 12% two years earlier. Management reframed SSG as a recurring, orchestration-led model with 74% recurring revenue, 85% renewal rate, and a stated plan to double revenue in three years. Heavy opex investment (platform, PS, people, process) is being made, with payback targeted within 3-5 years, and management flagged possible small inorganic deals.

financial_highlights.change: +29% YoY in USD; +37% in INR terms

financial_highlights.value: about 5% of SSG invoiced value not recognised as revenue; about $150M gap on $2.2B

financial_highlights.metric: Top 6 vendors share of SSG revenue

segments.name: Software
segments.commentary: About 40% of SSG revenue. Management cites industry shift to subscription and outcome-based consumption; software is 31% of global tech distribution per company citing Omdia.

segments.name: Cloud
segments.commentary: About 33% of SSG revenue. Management says cloud now grows 40-50% consistently; AWS relationship described as a strategic collaboration agreement (multibillion-dollar, about 5-year commitment, per AWS speaker).

segments.name: Security
segments.commentary: About 27% of SSG revenue. Managed security practice DigiGlass launched in India after Middle East; management says security is the area where growth has lagged potential.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.commentary: Under 1% of SSG revenue today; 500+ PS staff across 5+ delivery centres. Goal to scale PS 7x-10x over the next few years, with ecosystem delivery also scaling 7x-10x.

guidance_outlook: Revenue of about $5B in three years (FY29) for SSG, which management says is more than double the current base.
Gross margin of 5.5% to 6% for SSG, with a positive bias if professional services mix improves; PAT margin closer to 2% in the three-year period.
Renewal rate to reach 90% in 3 years and above 95% as a stated objective; 80%+ of renewals to be tracked in the system by FY28.
Recurring revenue share to rise to 85% in 3 years; ARR milestones and subscription mix to be reported quarterly.
SSG long-term aspiration of about 25% of group business; management says hardware growing 15-20% could keep SSG at 17-25% of mix.
Next CQ 2.0 module releases planned for September and December; investment programme payback targeted at 3-5 years, mostly opex (80-90%).
capex_capacity: Investments largely opex (80-90%) across platform, portfolio, professional services, process and people; capex limited to platforms, tools and AI CoE physical assets; investment expected for the next 3-5 years.
Five global captive delivery centres (CISS, built out of India); 1,000-person SSG team; 500+ PS team.
AI labs planned: two in India, one in Dubai and one in Singapore (Launchpad hub), with satellite launchpads per country in SESA.
Partner network around 10,000 partners; 130+ brands; relationships in 40+ markets; 10+ automation tools and 100+ accelerators.
Possible small inorganic acquisitions to fill capability gaps; not included in the investment figures presented.
demand_pricing: Management says SSG margin uplift from attaching services is about 60%, and that renewals and subscriptions carry a gross-margin spread rather than full invoice value under IFRS.
Management said gross margin growth lagged revenue growth due to product mix; PS and security are cited as under-penetrated areas to lift margin.
Competitive pressure: management acknowledged some distributors give away the 5.5-6% margin to win share, a reason for lower renewal rates in some categories.
Management cites India ICT CAGR near 11% and Middle East 8-10%; India cloud growth 25% (SME cloud 35-37%); Middle East cloud 18-20%.
Management says SSG's SME share is about 70% of transactions and 30% of customers, while enterprise deals may be a larger share of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross profit growing slower than revenue; is growth coming at the expense of margin?
qa_highlights.answer: SVK said it is partly product mix; target is 5.5-6% gross margin with positive bias. Hariharan said gross margin should grow in line with revenue over time as security and PS scale.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and balance sheet impact of SSG?
qa_highlights.answer: SVK said working capital intensity is similar to hardware: inventory is lower, but receivable days are longer; higher profitability lifts ROCE. Capex stays low; investments are mainly opex for 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why would renewal rates fall below 100% and why would margins persist from year 2?
qa_highlights.answer: Sayantan Dev said non-renewals mostly stem from poor customer adoption, hence the customer success team; Hariharan said distributors giving away margin are another cause. Year-2 margin is justified by lifecycle value added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term SSG share of revenue and profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Hariharan said the aspiration is about 25% of business over coming years, but with hardware growing 15-20% and software 30-35%, the ratio could stay 17-25%.

qa_highlights.question: How vulnerable is cloud and software to vendors selling direct to large enterprises?
qa_highlights.answer: Hariharan said large enterprises will be engaged directly by OEMs, but vendors increasingly depend on distributors across the lifecycle. SVK noted the disruption question has been raised for 20 years, while revenue grew 2.5x since listing.

qa_highlights.question: How much will professional services scale and what are the gaps?
qa_highlights.answer: Hariharan said PS is at about 2-3 on a 1-10 scale, aiming for 8-9, with PS and ecosystem delivery both aimed at 7-10x. Focus is on productised services, not custom or $1M+ bespoke deals; headcount additions are planned this year.

risks_watch: Gross margin of 5.5-6% depends on PS and security mix improving; current PS is under 1% of SSG revenue.
Opex-heavy investment (80-90% opex) over 3-5 years could weigh on profit; management flagged profit growth as a constraint.
Revenue recognition gap of about 5% between invoiced and recognised value, plus rising unbilled revenue and longer receivable days.
Renewal rate (85%) could plateau or fall with late-entrant competition and distributors cutting margins.
Top 6 vendors hold 70%+ of SSG revenue; concentration risk and possible vendor direct selling to large enterprises.
Withholding tax, transfer pricing for captive centres and data protection compliance across countries still in progress.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the SSG growth story and long-term targets, while candid about gaps (PS at 2-3 out of 10, security under-penetrated, margin mix still being built). Management was measured on financial targets, stressing that investments are opex-led and profit will not be compromised.
key_quotes: So what you see as revenue in the books, vis-a-vis what we invoice, there will be a 5% gap.
About 74 percentage of our last year revenue is recurring.
So, the mantra is own the platform, attach services, manage the life cycle and compound recurring revenue.
We're not going to be doing custom services. We are not going to be doing bespoke services.

adds.what: AI labs: two in India, one in Dubai, one in Singapore (Launchpad hub) with satellite launchpads
Investment programme mostly opex (80-90%) across platform, PS, people, process; capex limited to platforms, tools and AI CoE physical assets

growth.why: Management guides SSG to about $5B revenue in three years (more than double the $2.2B FY26 base, roughly 32% CAGR) at 5.5-6% gross margin, with PAT near 2%, but the call was an investor event rather than a quarterly results call and the plan rests on opex investment, new AI labs and a mix shift rather than specific capacity, orders or contracts with timing.
